summary: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967) and held posts at Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha as Reader and Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan, Sri Sadashiva Campus, as Principal (attested 1973).

M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, the University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner. He was a Professor of History, department head, and arts dean at the University of Mysore.

M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She served as a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990) and as Professor at King's College London (1990–2014), later joining University College London.

M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the Archaeological Survey of India, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Calicut, where he later served as Professor from circa 1978 to 1996.

M. S. A. Rao was an Indologist who studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held a post at the University of Delhi (~1955–1985) and positions at Pennsylvania and Syracuse universities.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied under M. N. Deshpande, at the University of Mysore, and at Savitribai Phule Pune University. He served as curator at Karnatak University and Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University (attested 1899), and Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1899).
M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Agoura High School, the Art Center College of Design, and under Seiren Matsunami.

M. Yamunacharya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. She studied at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities, later serving as Associate Professor and Asian Studies Director at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), among other international appointments.
Maanasa Visweswaran is an Indology and computational linguistics researcher who studied at and served as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Mabel Haynes Bode was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied under T. W. Rhys Davids, Cecil Bendall, and Edouard Müller-Hess, taking her PhD at Bern. She lectured in Pali at University College London and SOAS University of London.

Madan Mohan Malaviya was an Indian scholar and educator. He studied at Muir Central College, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Allahabad. He founded Banaras Hindu University in 1916 and served as its Vice Chancellor from 1919 to 1938.

Madeleine Biardeau was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religion. She studied at École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres, the University of Kerala, and under K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. She was Professor of Indian Religions at EPHE from circa 1967 to 1989.
Madhav Krishna Sharma was an Indologist who studied under C. Kunhan Raja and served as an Inspector for the Government of Rajasthan.
Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a Professor at the University of Michigan (attested 1976–2009).

Madhav Sadashiv Gore studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye at the University of Mumbai and at Columbia University School of Social Work. He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University from circa 1987 to 1990.
Madhu Khanna is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who held posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (both attested 2012).

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied geology and chemistry at Fergusson College and served as Associate Director and Director Emeritus of Research at the American Institute of Indian Studies between 1974 and 2005.

Madhusudan Gupta studied at and taught Ayurveda at Sanskrit College and University (~1826–1835). He also studied at and held a post at Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata (~1835–1856), working in Indology and related fields.
